Load a Laya engine

Source: R/engine.R
laya_engine.Rd

Loads an exported ONNX checkpoint into memory (about 1 to 1.5 GB of RAM) and returns an engine to pass to laya_predict() and friends. Create one and reuse it: loading takes several seconds, predictions are fast.

Usage

laya_engine(
  checkpoint = c("multilingual", "english", "typed-decisions"),
  model_dir = NULL,
  intra_op_threads = getOption("layaR.threads"),
  inter_op_threads = NULL,
  lang_temperatures = NULL
)

Arguments

checkpoint

Which checkpoint to load: "multilingual" (100+ languages, the default), "english" (English-optimized) or "typed-decisions" (fine-tuned for four specific workflows).

model_dir

Path to an exported checkpoint directory. Overrides the lookup by checkpoint (see laya_model_path()).

intra_op_threads, inter_op_threads

ONNX Runtime thread counts. NULL lets ONNX Runtime choose. The layaR.threads option sets the default for intra_op_threads.

lang_temperatures

Optional per-language calibration overrides, a named list such as list(fr = list(temperature = c(1.1, 1, 0.9))); see the Python SDK's lang_temperatures. They apply to calls made with a matching lang.

Value

A laya_engine object.

Details

Most code never needs this: the prediction functions default to laya_default_engine(), which loads the checkpoint named by the layaR.checkpoint option ("multilingual" by default) on first use and keeps it for the session.

Engines can't be sent to other processes. An engine restored with readRDS(), or used in a PSOCK worker (parallel::makePSOCKcluster(), future::multisession), reconnects to its model directory on first use, which loads the model again in that process (another 1 to 1.5 GB each).

Engines don't work across fork() (parallel::mclapply(), future::multicore): ONNX Runtime's thread pools don't survive it, so a forked child could hang. Using an engine in a forked child raises a laya_error_forked error instead. A single engine already runs one forward pass on several cores; for more throughput use laya_predict_batch(), or PSOCK workers that each load their own engine.

See also

laya_predict(), laya_engine_info(), laya_engine_close()

Examples

if (laya_model_available()) {
  engine <- laya_engine("multilingual", intra_op_threads = 2)
  engine
  laya_engine_close(engine)
}
